newsitem.title: UK: OPTIONS -Bund vols hold as EMU concerns dominate.
newsitem.headline: OPTIONS -Bund vols hold as EMU concerns dominate.

text.p: Implied volatility of Bund options on LIFFE stayed firm on Wednesday as the underlying futures market continued to dwell on concerns about a single European currency, traders said.
Traders said partial holidays in German on Thursday would curtail volumes but markets would remain nervous until after the second round of French elections on Sunday.

"Volatility initially started to recede on the (futures) market rallying in Europe on the open...but as we got to the highs of the day the market retreated and vol started to go slightly bid," a trader at GNI in London said.
In the July options on the September Bund futures, brokers quoted implied volatility of 99.50 straddles at around 5.70 percent compared with 5.67 percent at the close on Tuesday.
September volatility was quoted at about 5.65 percent compared with 5.50 percent.
September Bund futures were quoted at 99.60, down 13 basis points on the day after reaching up to a high of 99.92 in early trade.
A win by left-wing parties in French elections in the first round on Sunday left markets questioning France's commitment to get its fiscal house in shape for EMU.
"What we're seeing is Bund options volatility reasonably high compared to recent times," said a trader at French brokerage in London.
The trader at GNI said call spread trades were the order of the day, with three chunky trades dominating.

Paper bought 1,500 lots of a July 101.00-102.00 one-by-two call spread. They also bought 1,000 lots of the July 99.50-101.00 one-by-two call spread and sold 2,000 lots of the September 102.50-103.50 one-by-two call spread.

"They are the highlights so far today," the trader said. "Most people are reasonably well positioned. It's going to be quite difficult to spur the market into activity with a holiday in Germany tomorrow. Then we'll probably wait until Sunday until the election result." --Jacqueline Thorpe, International Bonds Unit +44 171 542 6176
